title: Passing an array of structures to a function

visuals.title: Match each idea to its meaning

pairs.meaning: Receives the original array and its count; changes are kept
The call: array name without [] and the number of records
The function may read the records but not change them
The function only gets the address of the array, so it cannot know the size
The marks member of record number i
No record matched, so there is no valid index

visuals.title: How an array of structures travels to a function

stages.name: 1. The call
stages.detail: main writes addBonus(cls, 3): the array name and the count.

stages.name: 2. No copy of the records
stages.detail: Only the address of the first record is passed. list is the same array as cls.

stages.name: 3. The loop
stages.detail: for (i = 0; i < n; i++) visits list[0] ... list[n-1], using list[i].member.

stages.name: 4. Back in main
stages.detail: The records were changed in place, so main sees the new values with no return needed.

goal: After this you can pass an array of structures and its count to functions that read, print, search and find the best record, and you know why the original array is changed.
warmup: A class teacher keeps one register with the records of 50 students. She hands the SAME register to the clerk to add bonus marks, and the next day to the coordinator to print the toppers. Nobody photocopies all 50 pages first. The register (array) goes to each person, along with a note saying how many pages are filled (the count).
definition: An array of structures is passed to a function like any array: write the array name in the call and give the parameter as Type list[] in the function header. The function receives the address of the first record, so no copy is made and the function works on the ORIGINAL array: changes stay after the function returns. The array does not carry its size, so the count n is passed as a second argument. Use const Type list[] when the function only reads the records.
howItWorks: Step through the trace. In addBonus the parameter list is not a copy of cls: it is the same array. So list[0].marks += 5 changes cls[0].marks in main. n is a normal int, so it IS a copy. Common jobs follow the same pattern. Read INTO the array: the function fills list[i].name and list[i].marks with cin and returns how many records it read. Print: a loop that shows each record, with const. Search: a loop that compares list[i].name with the key and returns the index i, or -1 when nothing matches. Best record: keep a variable best with the index of the best record so far, and update it whenever a better one appears. A menu connects them: a do-while loop reads a choice and a switch calls one function for each case. Remember that the array has a fixed size, so always keep n at most that size.

variations.when: The function must change the records (read input, add bonus, restock).
variations.example: void addBonus(Student list[], int n);  // addBonus(cls, 3);

variations.way: void f(const Student list[], int n)
variations.when: The function only reads (print, total, search, best).
variations.example: void printAll(const Student list[], int n);

variations.when: Search and best-record functions: give back the position, then use cls[idx].
variations.example:
int idx = findByName(cls, n, "Sara");
if (idx != -1) cout << cls[idx].marks;

variations.when: A function that fills the array tells main how many records it stored.
The function needs only one record, so it receives cls[i] as a structure (by value, reference or const reference).
One program offers many jobs; each case calls one function.

mistakes.error: error: too few arguments to function 'void printAll(const Student*, int)'
error: assignment of member 'Student::marks' in read-only object

mistakes.wrong: int count = sizeof(list) / sizeof(list[0]);   // inside the function
mistakes.right: Pass the count n as a parameter.
mistakes.error: The compiler accepts it, but inside the function list is only an address, so the result is wrong (not the real number of records). Always pass the count.

mistakes.wrong:
for (int i = 0; i <= n; i++)
    cout << list[i].name;
mistakes.right:
for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
    cout << list[i].name;
mistakes.error: No compiler error. The loop reads one record beyond the last one, which is out of bounds and gives garbage or a crash.

examTips: Say clearly: an array is passed by address, so the function changes the original array. No & is needed for arrays.
Always pass the count with the array. The function cannot find the size by itself.
Use const in the header of functions that only print, search or sum. It shows you know they do not modify the records.
For search, return the index and -1 for not found; check for -1 before using cls[idx].
For the best record keep the INDEX of the best so far (best = i), not just the marks, so you can print the name too.
romanSummary: Array of structures function ko normal array ki tarah jata hai: sirf array ka naam likhte hain, bracket nahi.
Function ko array ka address milta hai, copy nahi, is liye original array badal jata hai.
Array ka size function ko nahi pata hota, is liye count n alag se bhejna parta hai: printAll(cls, n).
Sirf parhna ho to const Student list[] likhein. Search mein index return karte hain, na milne par -1.
Menu program mein do-while aur switch use hota hai, har case mein ek function call hota hai.

quiz.prompt: Why do we pass the count n together with the array?
options: The function cannot know the array's size
The array would be copied otherwise
The compiler needs it for const
quiz.answer: The function cannot know the array's size
quiz.hint: The function gets only an address.
quiz.explanation: An array parameter is just an address, so the size must be sent separately.

quiz.prompt: How is an array of structures written in the call?
quiz.explanation: Only the array name is written in the call.

quiz.prompt: A function adds bonus marks to list[i].marks. What happens to the array in main?
quiz.explanation: The function works on the original array.

quiz.prompt: What should findByName return when the name is not in the list?
quiz.explanation: -1 is never a valid index, so it safely means not found.

quiz.prompt: When should the parameter be const Student list[]?
options: When the function only reads the records
When the function fills the array
quiz.answer: When the function only reads the records
quiz.explanation: const forbids changes, so use it only for read-only functions.
